profile.name: Areeb Ahmed
profile.title: Mechanical Engineer
profile.summary: Mechanical engineer with 3 years of experience designing, building and scaling carbon-capture hardware from concept to commissioning. Driven by climate tech: Direct Air Capture, electrolysis and sustainable energy systems.

highlights.label: DAC plant delivered on time and on budget

bullets: Building a CFD model in SimScale to determine pressure drop across a novel electrolyzer stack for CO₂ release.
Designing the CO₂ desorption skid of the single-cell plant in Autodesk Inventor for flexible operating points and cell prototyping, using a self-developed custom piping add-in.
Set up Autodesk Vault as the PDM system for custom and standard parts.
Integrated Vault with the company PLM and ERP systems through an Inventor dashboard and agentic workflows, keeping CAD and ERP data in sync and shortening design-to-execution time.
Led a 13-person multidisciplinary engineering team (process, electrical, mechanical) responsible for commercial-scale DAC engineering.
Scaled DAC systems from design to commercial deployment within cost and technical targets; delivered a 30 tCO₂/year plant on time and on budget.
Reduced energy consumption of Gen-2 systems by 10×.
Halved machine cost from Gen 1 to Gen 2 by simplifying the design and reducing part count, eliminating or replacing components.
Moved the design platform to Autodesk and introduced PLM/PDM practices for DAC reactors, including ERP and Vault integration.
Led mechanical design of the first-of-a-kind (FOAK) DAC plant.
Designed Gen 1 and Gen 2 DAC reactor structures to ASME Section VIII Div 1 for deep-vacuum operation, including bolted joints and gaskets for leak tightness.

Acted as piping engineer for the DAC pilot plant: designed instrument air, steam and condensate piping in AutoCAD Plant 3D to ASME B31.3 and B31.1, and selected and installed piping and plant equipment.
Acted as systems integrator for electrical components (cable routing, sensor placement).
Applied DFMA by incorporating feedback from fabrication technicians; coordinated with the civil EPC and used Navisworks for clash detection.
Managed mechanical installation and commissioning, completed within 3 weeks.
Designed and built thermal systems and custom heat exchangers for heating and cooling of sorbent filters; improved heat-exchanger performance by 15% through experimental testing and CFD validation.
Designed air intake and exhaust using ANSYS Fluent and ASHRAE principles, tripling the capture capacity of the same-generation machine and reducing reactor pressure drop by 1.5×.
Ran parametric CFD studies (ANSYS Fluent) to verify and optimise heating and cooling systems.
Sourced specialised components through suppliers and industry experts (TLV, Spirax Sarco).
Built Python (CoolProp) tools to model energy and steam demand of heat-integration options, e.g. heat pumps and heat and pressure losses in piping.
Supported fabrication, erection and maintenance of API 650 storage tanks.
Carried out dye-penetrant weld inspections on steam and process lines for an oil refinery.
Produced as-built piping isometrics for a palm oil refinery to support change management.

details: Coursework completed; master's thesis to follow.
